name: Nasal splint after rhinoplasty

lead: A nasal splint is the protective cover placed over the nose after rhinoplasty. It keeps the newly reshaped bones and cartilage from moving, so the nose heals in the shape the surgeon created.

The splint and tape hold the nose still and shield it from pressure and knocks during early healing. Internal splints, such as silastic or resorbable types, support the septum or cartilage from inside and are used in septal and nasal surgery. Studies of splints and packing are mostly in that surgery and compare bleeding, comfort and complications.

paras: The surgical team applies the tape and splint at the end of the operation, and the dressing is usually removed about a week later. It is worn only during early healing and is not something people buy or fit themselves. Internal splints are placed and removed by the surgeon.

Reported issues include discomfort, bacterial colonization with internal splints and, in one study, respiratory distress with totally occlusive packing compared with splints or sutures. Percutaneous osteotomy scars have also been described after rhinoplasty. Any problems with fit or breathing go back to the surgical team.

angle.text: After rhinoplasty, a splint and tape hold the reshaped nose still so it heals in the shape the surgeon created. It is usually removed after about a week. Patients and forum posters discuss it as part of protecting the surgical result.

lead: A nasal splint is a protective device placed over or inside the nose after surgery. After rhinoplasty, the surgeon typically applies tape and a custom-shaped splint to keep the nose still while the incisions heal, and the dressing is removed about one week after the procedure [1].

Internal splints and nasal packing are used in septal and nasal surgery, and studies have compared them with transseptal sutures and with no packing in terms of bleeding, comfort and complications [2][3][4]. Materials have included silastic sheets, rapidly setting conformable external splint material and resorbable internal splints [5][6][7].
infobox: About one week for the external dressing [1]
External splint, internal silastic or resorbable splint [2][5][7]

paras: In a rhinoplasty, the nose is prepared with paper tape and then covered by a shaped splint to protect tender tissues; a stent inside the nose may also be used [1]. A survey of facial plastic surgeons examined practice patterns in the perioperative care of septorhinoplasty patients, indicating that splinting practices vary between surgeons [8].

Specialised splints have been described for particular problems, such as a dynamic nostril splint used in nasal tip surgery in cleft patients and a resorbable internal splint used in unilateral cleft lip nasal repair to shield the alar cartilage from scar forces [7][9].

A randomised trial in 95 patients examined packing types and a silastic splint after routine nasal surgery [2]. In a comparison of 150 septoplasty patients, totally occlusive nasal packing was associated with an increased risk of respiratory distress during recovery from anesthesia compared with internal splints and transseptal sutures [3]. Another study looked at the timing of internal splint use with respect to bacterial colonization, complications and patient discomfort [10].

Trials and comparative studies have examined nasal packs, internal splints and transseptal sutures after septal surgery [2][3][4][10], a prospective study evaluated a conformable, rapidly setting splint material [5], and a survey described practice patterns among facial plastic surgeons [8]. These studies mainly address complications and comfort after nasal and septal surgery rather than long-term aesthetic outcomes of rhinoplasty.
Splints appear in this wiki as part of the recovery phase of nose surgery, which is a common topic in looksmaxxing discussion. No forum material is cited here.
